sections.history: Thirunagai, the Nagapattinam of the Alvars, is one of the 108 Divya Desams and one of the shrines of Chola Nadu, the Kaveri delta country that runs down to the sea here. Thirumangai Alvar sang its lord in the Periya Thirumozhi, in verses where he takes the voice of a young woman lost in the beauty of the god and finds that beauty greater than that of the lords of other sacred places. Tradition credits the temple to the Medieval Cholas in the late eighth century, and the Nayaks of Thanjavur later added to it, so that the coastal town, long a port of many faiths, has kept its Vishnu shrine through more than a thousand years.
sections.architecture: A five-tiered rajagopuram rises over the entrance, and a granite wall encloses the shrines. In the sanctum Vishnu stands as Neelamega Perumal, a tall image holding the mace, facing east beneath the Soundarya Vimanam; the festival image is Soundararajan, and the Goddess Soundaryavalli has her own shrine, with Gajalakshmi as her festival form. The temple tank is the Sara Pushkarini, and pillared halls lead the devotee from the gateway to the sanctum.
sections.legends: The sthala purana tells that Adisesha, king of the Nagas and the serpent couch of Vishnu, worshipped the lord here, and local tradition holds that the town takes its name — Nagai, Nagapattinam — from him. The sages Markandeya and Dhruva, and Bhudevi the Earth Goddess, are also said to have received the darshan of the lord at this shrine, and his name, the king of beauty, recalls the form in which he appeared to them.
sections.festivals: The chariot festival in the Tamil month of Chittirai is the temple's greatest occasion, drawing the town into the streets. At Panguni Uthiram the celestial wedding of Soundararajan and Soundaryavalli is celebrated, and in Aadi the lord is brought to a hall to hear the hymns of Thirumangai Alvar. Vaikunta Ekadashi is kept with devotion.
sections.experience: The temple stands within the busy town, a short way from the harbour and the shore, and its quiet courts are a counterpoint to the bustle outside. Come to see the tall standing lord, then the festival Soundararajan, and read Thirumangai Alvar's verses on his beauty — this is a shrine whose very name is an invitation to look.

visit.timings: Open daily with morning and evening darshan sessions and a midday closure; the Chittirai chariot festival and Vaikunta Ekadashi are busiest. Confirm current timings before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear removed before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is restricted in and around the sanctum; follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.gettingThere: The temple is in Nagapattinam town, on the coast of the Kaveri delta. Nagapattinam has a railway station with connections towards Thanjavur and Tiruchirappalli, and good road links with Thiruvarur, Karaikal and Velankanni; the nearest airport is Tiruchirappalli.
